reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E3 shows inverse Hall-Petch and tribofilm formation in a different HEA (CoCrFeMnNi) at room temperature, not in FeNiCrCoCu at high temperature. E1 and E2 discuss hardness and wear of HEA composites under different conditions, providing no evidence for pre-annealing-induced nanocrystallization or its effect on tribofilm evolution in the target alloy and regime.
premises: Pre-annealing FeNiCrCoCu coating at ~500 °C induces nanocrystalline features (nanotwins/grain refinement)
Nanocrystalline initial structure promotes formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline tribofilm during high-temperature sliding
Ultra-nanocrystalline tribofilm exhibits inverse Hall-Petch behavior, lowering effective shear strength
Lowered shear strength reduces material removal, crack initiation, and plastic deformation, enhancing wear resistance
These mechanisms operate in the 500–800 °C regime under limited oxidation
